title: Pediatric urologist visit
what: The doctor examines your child's genitals and urinary system and checks that they are developing normally.
why: At routine checkups for boys, and for problems with peeing, wetting, or swelling or pain in the scrotum.
duration: usually 15 to 30 minutes; you get advice right away
tell_doctor: What bothers you, and since when
How often your child pees, and if there are accidents

prepare.title: Talk to your child
prepare.text: Calmly explain that the doctor will take a look and it does not hurt. Do not use the doctor as a threat.

prepare.title: Hygiene
prepare.text: Usual washing in the morning, with no special products.

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: If the doctor ordered a urine test or ultrasound beforehand, have it done before the visit.

bring: Past urine tests and ultrasounds, if you have them
A diaper or spare underwear for a little one
steps: The doctor asks you about the concerns and your child's development
Your child undresses below the waist
The doctor examines the genitals, sometimes standing and lying down
The belly is felt if needed
The doctor explains what was seen and gives advice
feel: Your child may feel shy or cry. You are there. That is normal
after: If an ultrasound or tests were ordered, have them done and come back
red_flags: Sudden severe pain or swelling in the scrotum: see a doctor urgently, call emergency services

faq.q: Should I pull back my baby's foreskin?
faq.a: No. Never force it back. Your doctor will explain how to care for it.

faq.q: At what age should a boy see a urologist?
faq.a: Usually at routine checkups. If there are symptoms, at any age.

reminders.text: Pediatric urologist visit tomorrow. Bring your child's documents and past test results.
